name: PayFast

status.webhook_verification: ITN (Instant Transaction Notification) POST to notify_url — FOUR mandatory checks: (1) recompute MD5 signature over the RECEIVED-order fields (PHP urlencode, +passphrase if set) vs posted 'signature'; (2) source-IP allowlist DNS-resolved from www/sandbox/w1w/w2w.payfast.co.za; (3) postback the untouched payload to /eng/query/validate and require body 'VALID'; (4) merchant_id matches AND amount_gross within 0.01 of expected. Must return HTTP 200. A redirect return is NEVER proof of payment.

credentials_required.label: Merchant ID
credentials_required.note: PayFast dashboard → Settings → Integration. Separate values per environment (sandbox vs live).

credentials_required.label: Merchant Key
credentials_required.note: PayFast dashboard → Settings → Integration. Separate per environment.

credentials_required.label: Security Passphrase (Salt)
credentials_required.note: Optional but REQUIRED for subscriptions/tokenization. If set on the account it MUST be appended to EVERY signature, both checkout and ITN, or the hash won't match.

test_credentials.note: Widely-cited PayFast sandbox demo credentials — rotate/regenerate your own at sandbox.payfast.co.za (login by email, generated instantly, no KYC). Sandbox simulates the hosted page and always succeeds.

sandbox.notes: Sandbox has NO public test card numbers — it simulates the hosted payment page (choose the outcome) rather than taking real card input. Recurring/subscriptions are NOT testable in sandbox (once-off only).

pain_points.problem: Signature mismatch — the #1 PayFast integration failure
pain_points.cause: JavaScript encodeURIComponent() is NOT PHP urlencode(): it leaves ! ' ( ) * ~ unescaped, uses %20 for spaces (PHP uses +), and casing can differ. Signing with it produces a hash PayFast rejects.
pain_points.mitigation: Use ONE canonical phpUrlEncode() (encodeURIComponent then replace !→%21 '→%27 (→%28 )→%29 *→%2A ~→%7E and %20→+, uppercase hex) for BOTH checkout signing and ITN verify. Ship a signature-debug tool that returns the exact hashed param string.

pain_points.cause: Checkout must sign fields in PayFast's DOCUMENTED order (not alphabetical, not insertion order), but the ITN must be signed in the order the fields were RECEIVED. Mixing them up breaks the hash.
pain_points.mitigation: Hardcode the documented checkout order; for the ITN, parse the raw body preserving received order and sign that. Never re-order the ITN fields.

pain_points.problem: Passphrase handling is asymmetric or forgotten
pain_points.cause: The passphrase (Salt) is per-merchant and optional, but if it's set on the account it MUST be appended (&passphrase=urlencode(value)) to every signature. Omitting it on one side (or adding it when unset) breaks the hash.
pain_points.mitigation: Treat passphrase as a nullable per-merchant credential and apply it symmetrically to checkout AND ITN signatures — append only when non-blank.

pain_points.problem: Legitimate '0' values get stripped from the signature
pain_points.cause: Filtering blank fields on JS truthiness drops '0' — but subscription cycles=0 (indefinite) and other zero values are valid and MUST be signed.
pain_points.mitigation: Filter on '' / null / undefined (blank-ness after trim), NEVER on truthiness, so '0' survives into the signature.

pain_points.problem: Trusting the browser return / skipping ITN validation checks
pain_points.cause: Treating the return_url redirect (or an unvalidated ITN) as proof of payment lets an attacker spoof a 'paid' outcome.
pain_points.mitigation: Only a fully-validated ITN is proof: enforce all four checks (signature, source-IP allowlist via DNS, postback expecting 'VALID', amount+merchant_id match) non-bypassably, return 200 immediately and process asynchronously.

pain_points.problem: ITN rejected by hardcoded source-IP allowlist
pain_points.cause: PayFast rotates the IPs its ITN servers send from; a static IP allowlist eventually blocks real notifications.
pain_points.mitigation: DNS-resolve the valid hosts (www/sandbox/w1w/w2w.payfast.co.za) at request time and test membership — never hardcode IPs.

pain_points.cause: Pre-encoding return_url/cancel_url/notify_url before they reach the signer, then encoding again, corrupts the hash.
pain_points.mitigation: Pass raw URLs to the signer and urlencode exactly once inside phpUrlEncode().

sdks.node: none official — REST/self-sign (build the form + MD5 signature yourself)
sdks.php: payfast/payfast-php-sdk (PHP 8.1+; the official CMS plugins are the reference implementation)

notes: South Africa only, ZAR only. Payment is a redirect: render a signed hidden form POSTing to /eng/process; PayFast hosts the page; the outcome arrives via ITN. There is NO per-transaction status poll — the ITN is the source of truth. Refunds via dashboard + API; recurring via subscription_type=1 (recurring) or =2 (tokenization/Payvault ad-hoc charges). Signature is MD5 (lowercase hex) — the single most error-prone part; get phpUrlEncode + field order + passphrase exactly right.

verification.verified_notes: Signed checkout form verified live against the sandbox — PayFast accepted the MD5 signature and returned a 302 to a real payment session. CRITICAL: if a Salt Passphrase is set on the account it MUST be appended to the signature (a set-but-omitted passphrase = guaranteed mismatch); URL-encoding is PHP-style (spaces '+', uppercase hex).
unverified_fields: refund API endpoint path (verify before build)
full ITN round-trip (needs a public notify_url)
